question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
The evidence supports a "six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute" opt-out period [621/2025 §33(2)(b)]; the same appears in [551/2024 §33(2)(b)].

- This concerns National Building Research Organisation staff offered employment in the new Institute, not a general "offered position" rule [621/2025 §33(2)(a)–(b)].
- Newest text: 621/2025 GS (2025-07-17); 551/2024 GS (2024-09-03).

Caveats: The evidence was judged incomplete — if your question concerns a different appointment/transfer clause (e.g. a shorter acceptance period), that provision is missing and I cannot confirm it.

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
Not less than 30 days before the current licence expires: the renewal application must be submitted to the Director-General "not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration of the licence previously issued" [657/2025 §6(1)].

- The same clause text appears in Bill 007/2026 (presented 2026-01-20); the 2025 text is from the Gazette version (2025-12-12) [657/2025 §6(1); 007/2026 §6].

Caveats: The licence "duration" itself is in §4, which is only outlined here, so I can't state the licence term.

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
Notice of dishonour may be given "in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means" that sufficiently identify the bill and intimate it was dishonoured by non-acceptance or non-payment [601/2025 §8].

- The electronic route requires the means to "sufficiently identify the bill" and state the dishonour ground [601/2025 §8].
- This replaces section 49(5) of the principal Ordinance [601/2025 §8].

Caveats: The evidence is the GS version (601/2025, 2025-06-04); the same text appears in 612/2025 (Bill, 2025-06-17) and earlier bills, but only 601's clause text is quoted here. 612/2025 is the newest matching bill.

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The 2026 Bill (newest, Bill dated 2026-06-25; GS dated 2026-06-11) lets the Society "take and hold any property, movable or immovable" vested in it by "purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or otherwise," held "for the purpose of this Act" and subject to its section 7 rules [047/2026 §13]. It may obtain land or buildings by "purchase, rent construct, renovate" and dispose of them as the Council determines [047/2026 §6(a)].

- With those assets it has "power to sell, mortgage, lease, exchange, or otherwise dispose of the same" [047/2026 §13].
- It may hold property under "any lawful trust" to promote its objects [047/2026 §6(f)].

Caveats: GS and Bill text of §13/§6 is identical; older bills (2021, 2010) have similar wording but are superseded.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The long title is amended by replacing "freight forwarders, non-vessel operating common carriers, and container operators" with "freight forwarders and non-vessel operating common carriers", dropping the container operators reference [658/2025 §2].

- The substituted wording removes ", and container operators" from the listed categories [658/2025 §2].
- The same clause appears identically in Bill 005/2026 (2026-01-20) [658/2025 §2].
- §3 separately shortens the Act's name itself to the "Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders and Non-Vessel Operating Common Carriers Act" [658/2025 §3].

Caveats: Evidence is from the GS version (658/2025, 2025-12-12), stated to be identical in Bill 005/2026; the long title text is quoted with irregular capitalisation in the source.

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation) Bill, No. 055/2026, presented on 27 July 2026, incorporates the Foundation to pursue economic and rural resource development objectives [055/2026 §1][043/2026 §3].

- Objects include "developing, promoting, establishing, expanding or modernising all economic sectors in Sri Lanka" [043/2026 §3(a)].
- Also covers "vocational training, technical education" for rural youth and adults [043/2026 §3(b)], micro-entrepreneurship for "unemployed women and marginalised groups" [043/2026 §3(g)], and soil conservation guidance [043/2026 §3(i)].
- It becomes a body corporate with perpetual succession, able to sue and be sued [043/2026 §2(1)].

Caveats: The earlier Gazette version 043/2026 (15 June 2026) matches; 055/2026 spells the title "Recourses" in its heading.

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
The evidence does show an age disqualification: a person is disqualified from appointment to the Board if they "is over seventy years of age" [613/2025 §9(i)].

- Section 9 lists this among other disqualifications from appointment as a member of the Board [613/2025 §9].
- The same text appears in 594/2025 (GS, 2025-05-27); the Bill version is 613/2025 (2025-06-17) [613/2025 §9].

Caveats: The passage covers disqualification from appointment; it does not say whether a member is removed on turning 70 while serving, so that is missing.

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The evidence does not give a settlement day. The clause only says debts and liabilities "existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act" "shall be paid by the body corporate hereby constituted" [009/2026 §12] — no deadline is stated.

- The wording is the same in the 2021 bill [095/2021 §12], so neither fixes a date.
- Note the bill title in the evidence is "Indira Cancer Charitable Trust (Incorporation)" (GS, 2026-02-05) [009/2026 §12], not "Act".

Caveats: The clause text is all we have; any payment deadline may be missing from these extracts.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The amended definition is “the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department, appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act” [494/2024 §6], which replaces the old “Controller” definition; the same substitution appears in the 2025 versions [595/2025 §2; 620/2025 outline §6].

- All references to “Controller”/“Rubber Controller” in the Act and other written law read as “Director-General” [595/2025 §2(1)].
- In other documents they read as “Director-General of the Rubber Development Department” [595/2025 §2(2)].

Caveats: The full text of §6 is quoted only in 494/2024; 595/2025 and 620/2025 show §6 only in the bill outline.

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
The Chiththa bill defines "qualified auditor" as either an individual accountant holding a practising certificate, or a firm whose resident partners each hold one [172/2022 §10(4)].

- Individual: a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka or any other institute established by law, who "possesses a certificate to practice as an Accountant" issued by that institute's Council [172/2022 §10(4)(a)].
- Firm: a firm of Accountants whose resident partners each meet that membership and certificate-of-practice requirement [172/2022 §10(4)(b)].
- The auditor is appointed by the Auditor General under Article 154 of the Constitution [172/2022 §10(3)].

Caveats: The evidence is the GS version dated 2022-01-31, not a presented Bill; identical text also appears in 175/2022.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
The evidence does support a basic procedure, though not the full step-by-step detail: under the proposed new section 38A, the Commission computes fares by a formula it determines, and providers must display a fare list on the vehicle.

- Commission: computes fares "in accordance with the formula determined by the Commission from time to time", adhering to the "national policy relating to transportation fares approved by Parliament", and specifies them by "Order published in the Gazette"; it also determines the formula after "considering the written representations of the relevant stakeholders" [577/2025 §19; 592/2025 §5].
- Commission: publishes fare lists "in the official website of the Commission" and may inspect providers' compliance [577/2025 §19].
- Providers: prepare a list "in accordance with such lists published in such website" and display it "at any conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle"; failure is "guilty of an offence under section 40" [549/2024 §19].

Caveats: The evidence doesn't state the formula itself, the section 40 penalty, or display rules for non-omnibus services; the newest text is bill 577/2025 (GS, 2025-04-07), with near-identical wording in 549/2024.

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
The magistrate must monitor the centre **without giving advance notice**, visiting monthly, interviewing suspects, and inspecting detention records [078/2026 §33(1)(a)–(c)].

- A magistrate before whom a suspect was first produced may also visit and exercise the interview and inspection powers [078/2026 §33(2)].
- The centre's authority must give "prompt and unimpeded access" [078/2026 §33(3)].
- If torture or cruel/inhuman treatment is observed or alleged, the magistrate "shall forthwith make an order" for examination by a Judicial Medical Officer and shall report it under section 31 if satisfied on reasonable grounds [078/2026 §33(4)–(5)].

Caveats: Section 31's content is not in the evidence, so its consequences are unclear.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
The evidence does not support an answer: no passage in this corpus states the remedy for a company whose name has been struck off, nor the effect on its former assets.

- The Companies (Amendment) provisions here only cover "Registrar's power to grant extension" of time to furnish information or produce documents, with fines for non-compliance [582/2025 §16; 541/2024 §14].
- Nothing on restoration, re-registration, or vesting of property appears in the supplied text.

Caveats: The passages labelled §17 and §15 concern a different amendment (principal enactment s.487) and do not address this question.

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the amendment, a person convicted of an offence under Section 23r faces a fine "not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees", plus "a fine of five thousand rupees for each day" the offence continues after conviction [032/2026 §18].

- The fine is imposed "on conviction before the Magistrate having jurisdiction" [032/2026 §18].
- This replaces the earlier range of "not less than rupees ten thousand and not exceeding rupees one hundred thousand" and daily "rupees five hundred" [032/2026 §18].

Caveats: The evidence is a Bill version (2026-05-06), and the same text appears in 026/2026; committee-stage amendments are not included.

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
The list is changed by substituting "heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium or methamphetamine" for the existing words "heroin or cocaine or morphine or opium" in section 54A(1)(a) — i.e. methamphetamine is added [068/2026 §2]. For manufacturing drugs in Groups A–E other than those five, the new offence carries "a fine not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees" and/or "imprisonment ... not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years", on conviction by the High Court without a jury [068/2026 §2].

- The Third Schedule is also amended to insert Cannabis items 26A and 26B after item 26 in Group B, Part I [068/2026 §5].
- Same text appears in the earlier Gazette version, 062/2026 (2026-08-24) [062/2026 §2].

Caveats: The titles are "Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs (Amendment)" — the Bill is 068/2026 (2026-09-08) and the GS is 062/2026 (2026-08-24); both versions match on these clauses.

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
Partially answerable: the evidence does quote the Section 5 amendment, but only in the 2026-03-03 GS version (also in 023/2026) — it changes dates in paragraph (c) and adds a new paragraph (d).

- Paragraph (c): "January 1, 2024," becomes "on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to April 1, 2026," and "sixty million rupees." becomes "sixty million rupees; or" [017/2026 §3].
- Paragraph (d), added: for periods "on or after April 1, 2026," four-quarter aggregate turnover must "not exceed thirty-six million rupees" [017/2026 §3].
- Paragraph (b) only loses "or" (punctuation), no figure change [017/2026 §3].

Caveats: paragraph (d) reads as a registration/exemption-type condition under Section 5, not a free-standing turnover limit; the Bill text of §3 (023/2026, 2026-03-17) is not quoted here, so I cannot confirm whether the Bill and GS differ.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
The amendment raises one retirement age from "sixty-one years" to "sixty-three years" and sets the retirement age for "all other Judges and Magistrates" at "sixty-two years" [058/2026 §3].

- This substitutes the age in subsection (3) and replaces subsection (4) of section 6 [058/2026 §3].
- The new subsection (4) applies "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355)" [058/2026 §3].
- Text is identical in the GS (2026-08-07) and the Bill (2026-08-18) version [058/2026 §3].

Caveats: The clause does not say which judges fall under subsection (3); that requires the principal Act, which is not in the evidence.

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
The 2025 Bill is **596/2025, Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation)** (Bill, 2025-05-08; the earlier Gazette version is 581/2025, GS, 2025-04-10).

- On commencement, members "shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession" under that name [596/2025 §2].
- Short title: the "...Foundation (Incorporation) Act, No. of 2025" [596/2025 §1].

Caveats: Only these two versions appear; the Act number and any committee-stage changes are not in the evidence.

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 059/2026, the **Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) - Bill** (Bill, dated 2026-08-04), repeals the 2009 Act.

- It states: "The Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 is hereby repealed" [059/2026 §2].
- Its short title is the "Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Act" [059/2026 §1].
- An earlier GS version, Bill 036/2026 (GS, 2026-05-15), has identical text [036/2026].

Caveats: The evidence does not describe the 2009 Act's contents beyond its title, so the claim that it created the Chief of Defence Staff post rests on the bill's title and summary, not clause text.

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 bill is the **National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment)** Bill, which amends the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016 [604/2025 §2]. The presented Bill is dated 2025-06-03; the corresponding Gazette version is 586/2025 (2025-05-20) [604/2025 §1][586/2025].

- It replaces s.3(1) to set "twenty-seven thousand rupees" monthly ("one thousand eighty rupees" daily) from 1 April 2025 to 31 December 2025, rising to "thirty thousand rupees" ("one thousand two hundred") from 1 January 2026 [604/2025 §2].
- It treats certain budgetary relief allowances as part of the minimum wage and consolidates them into existing wages [604/2025 §3].

Caveats: The Bill and GS texts appear identical; committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
The 2025 bill is **Bill 642/2025, Betting and Gaming Levy (Amendment) - Bill (2025-10-21)**, which amends the Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988 [642/2025]. An earlier Gazette version, **640/2025 GS (2025-10-02)**, contains the same amending clauses [640/2025 §2].

- It changes the Section 2 rates: "ten per centum", "fifteen per centum" for years from 1 April 2023 to before 1 October 2025, and "eighteen per centum" from 1 October 2025 [640/2025 §2(1)].
- It doubles the dollar charge from "United States Dollars fifty" to "United States Dollars one hundred" [640/2025 §2(2)].

Caveats: The 642/2025 text clauses are not in the evidence; rate details come from 640/2025 §2, which appears to match.

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
Bill 056/2026, the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) Bill (2026-07-22), amends the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No. 47 of 1956 — the same text also appears in 044/2026 (GS, 2026-06-25).

- It raises three penalties from "ten thousand rupees" to "one hundred thousand rupees" [056/2026 §2] [056/2026 §3] [056/2026 §4].
- Higher amounts apply only to offences committed after it comes into operation [056/2026 §5].

Caveats: The evidence shows only penalty increases, not other changes to the 1956 rules.

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) Bill** (Bill 650/2025, presented 2025-11-14) amends the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008 [650/2025 §2].

- It shortens the maximum tax holiday from "twenty-five years" to "ten years" [650/2025 §2].
- It replaces section 3 with a new identification/cost-benefit procedure, including a Ministry of Finance recommendation "within one month" [650/2025 §3].
- It adds ex-post monitoring and penalties, with a "one month" show-cause period before sanctions [650/2025 §4].

Caveats: An identical text also appears as 643/2025 [650/2025 §2]. The 2008 Act is described as "as last amended by Act, No. 12 of 2011" [650/2025 §2].

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
The Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution, Bill 065/2026 (presented 2026-08-18), proposes it; a Gazette version, 057/2026 (2026-08-07), carries the same title [065/2026 §1].

- It amends Article 107 so Supreme Court judges retire at "sixty-seven years" and Court of Appeal judges at "sixty-five years" [065/2026 §2].
- The Chief Justice retires at 67 or after "six years" in office, "whichever occurs earlier" [065/2026 §2].
- Article 137's cap rises from "not more than nineteen other Judges" to "not more than twenty four" [065/2026 §3].

Caveats: The evidence labels it "Twenty Second"; I cannot confirm the ordinal count of past amendments.
